items.requirement: Sized for about 49.7 A: the board's draw from the pack at the 6.0 V floor with the four TPS55285 at 6.35 A, nominal at an assumed 90 %. Round 1 sized both for 12.23 A (V90). No pack disconnect passed round 1: its one shortlisted candidate, R5460N212AF-TR-FE, failed the open balance lead (V107) in FU-B1, and FU-B3 found none. Answered under Raised by P1: V295: As V294: 3.3 V a cell under load is the lowest trip, the threshold set above it by the IC's accuracy band. V95's ±75 mV, round 1's R5460 figure, is no requirement (owner, 2026-10-02) V297: One IC does the pack disconnect, the pack overcurrent protection, the bench pack balance lead and the pack temperature, selected in FU-2F (owner, 2026-10-02) V301: 10 µA stays, with an operator wake contact for a start from the pack alone. The open-lead behaviour may rest on the IC's undervoltage logic, an inference. A bench test confirms it before the pages call V107 met: mid wire open, with and without a charger, and first cell attach (owner, 2026-10-02)

items.function: overvoltage protection; reverse-polarity protection; inrush limiting
items.requirement: The DC input's overvoltage threshold, non-destructive (owner, 2026-09-30): round 1 left the overvoltage protection without a part. FU-B3 did not requalify the LM74800QDRRRQ1 for the reverse-polarity protection and the inrush limiting. Answered under Raised by P1: V299: Yes, as a current limitation. After a trip, a source between the release, 18.58 to 19.81 V, and 20.0 V stays cut off until it falls below the release, and the board runs from the pack. The DC input range stays 12 to 20 V. Firmware does not take the DC input as selected because it is present (owner, 2026-10-02)

items.requirement: Switches each of the 20 ports from 0.8 V (V55) to 8.4 V. The TPS259474LRPWR takes VIN only from 2.7 V. Answered under Raised by P1: V126: Only while the port is off, with the pin up to 12 V. While it is on, the switch conducts both ways: a braking servo drives current back into the rail, and a diode in the path would leave the servo's supply to rise until it fails. An ESC's BEC on an enabled port feeds the rail too; it is used with its BEC wire off, a current limitation (owner, 2026-10-02) V133: The capacitance is not known. The 2.35 A peak, the rail's 6.35 A limit less the 4.0 A two synchronised ports may draw, is a reported figure, not a pass or fail requirement (owner, 2026-10-02) V282: From 0.8 V the switch turns on and carries the port's current. The 3.0 A and the 570 mV this question names apply from 5.0 V up; below 5.0 V the drop is a reported figure, not a requirement (owner, 2026-10-01) V302: Yes. The search covers topologies that split the function across parts: a load switch from 0.5 V with separate reverse blocking, current limit and 20 V protection (owner, 2026-10-02) V312: A research run names the switch (TLP3545A first) and its current limit (INA301A1IDGKR on the port shunt first) as functions and verifies each, with the servo supply temperature latch's enable gate and power-up reset, before FU-2P56. No reverse-blocking part: V126 (owner, 2026-10-02)

Answered under Raised by P1: V279: 72.0 °C beside a servo converter and 66.25 °C beside the adjustable supply's converter: the junction stays at 125 °C or below at the 8 A typical inductor clamp. At 50 °C ambient without a heatsink a rail then holds about 2.47 A at 8.4 V from 6.0 V before it trips (owner, 2026-10-02) V281: 33 °C/W, the datasheet's RθJA on TI's 4-layer 2 oz EVM (SLVSI72A 5.3). items.requirement: FU-2B1 refutes the SLS XTRON pack on its discharge floor and its temperature. The maker's safety notes (REV.1.06, section 4) set 3.3 V a cell under load and 3.75 V at rest; its guide makes preheating mandatory below 18 °C for loads above 5C (15 A). The board's floor is 3.3 V a cell, and below 18 °C the pack delivers 15 A or less (owner, 2026-10-02). Answered under Raised by P1: V294: 3.3 V a cell under load, 6.6 V for the pack; it replaces F9's 3.0 V. The protector's undervoltage threshold sits above 3.3 V by its accuracy band, so 3.3 V is the lowest trip. The pack path stays sized at 6.0 V: 52.1 A nominal at a 5.8 V bus, rated 60 A (owner, 2026-10-02) V296: Below 18 °C at the pack's NTC, firmware lowers the TPS55285 current limits so the pack delivers 15 A or less (90 W at 6.0 V). The DC input keeps its full power. No part of its own (owner, 2026-10-02) V307: Yes, whatever a run returns: a fixed input of the owner. items.function: input transient clamp (TVS on the DC input and on the pack input)
items.requirement: No part in FU-2B1; P2 returned no entry for it. The reverse-polarity protection, the overvoltage protection, the inrush limiting and the source selection survive 60 V for 10 µs only behind the clamp: TVS2701DRBR clamps to 35.7 V at 27 °C and 37.3 V at 125 °C. The clamp is the power input's protection, researched in stage 1, with TVS2701DRBR as its first candidate (owner, 2026-10-02). Behind the overvoltage cut-off the bus sees the clamp voltage for 3.98 µs typical, 5.4 µs maximum, plus the MOSFETs' gate-discharge time, against the TPS55285's 27 V absolute maximum. Answered under Raised by P1: V308: A second clamp on the bus behind the cut-off, ahead of the TPS55285, holds their input pins at or under 27 V. A P2-P4 follow-up of R5 and R7 researches it before FU-2P56, and states how the BQ40Z80 pack pins stay at or under 35 V (owner, 2026-10-02)

items.requirement: A second clamp on the bus behind the LM74800 overvoltage cut-off, ahead of the four TPS55285, holds their input pins at or under 27 V (their absolute maximum) while the input clamp TVS2701DRBR holds the input at 35.7 V (27 °C) to 37.3 V (125 °C) for the cut-off's 3.98 µs typical, 5.4 µs maximum plus the MOSFETs' gate discharge (V308, owner, 2026-10-02). items.function: Port supply switch; Port supply current limit (new)
items.requirement: Two functions a port, 20 a board: the switch, a TLP3545A(TP1,F photorelay first, its MOSFET output in the C connection (both FU-2G verifiers confirmed it, and only the inrush check read 'not read'); its current limit, an INA301A1IDGKR on the R8 port shunt first, which pulls the switch's drive low at 4.30 to 4.51 A and holds it while the port's enable is high (V123). The switch conducts both ways while on, so a braking servo's current returns to the rail, and blocks the pin up to 12 V only while off: no reverse-blocking part (V126). Each function gets its own requirement list from V122 to V127 and V282: 3.0 A and the 570 mV drop from 5.0 V up, on from 0.8 V, off within 5 ms, 5 mA off-state. The inrush peak of 2.35 A is a reported figure, not a pass or fail requirement (V133). Name each part by its orderable number (V312, owner, 2026-10-02)

found_values.value: The INA228 of the cabled shunt path fills BENCH page 0x20 registers 0 (voltage) and 1 (current) whenever it answers; the ESC telemetry fills them only when no monitor answers. The two shunt paths replace each other, so one INA228 answers per test. How the firmware tells which path is cabled is not stated. Applied to Motor monitor as 'reading of record'
found_values.source: checkout 68adf31: hardware/docs/IOBoard.md, Measurement intro (the two paths replace each other, owner 2026-09-25); firmware/iomcu/src/main.c:714-725 (telemetry is the only source on the bring-up module); docs/OpenYGE.md:380-381

found_values.value: Trip at each path's rated current: 150 A onboard (F2, continuous) and 300 A external (V50, peak for 30 s). On the INA228 at ADCRANGE 1 both are 30.00 mV (150 A x 200 uOhm, 300 A x 100 uOhm), SOVL 24,000 counts of 1.25 uV. With the BAS-M-R0001-E-5.0 at +5 % the external trip falls to 285.7 A; with the BVR at +1 % the onboard trip falls to 148.5 A. Applied to Motor monitor as 'overcurrent alert threshold'
found_values.source: Research.md F2, V48, V50; IOBoard.md:458, :462; INA228 SLYS021A 7.6.1.13 (SOVL 1.25 uV/LSB at ADCRANGE 1), https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/ina228.pdf

found_values.value: Answered under V288 (owner, 2026-10-01): an operator-set limit on the LIMITS page for each temperature the board reads. The onboard shunt sensor reads to at least 100 degC, the terminal temperature at which the BVR states its P>100 degC rating (6 W). Applied to Onboard shunt temperature sensor as 'range'
found_values.source: Research.md V288; BVR Issue 12-September-2024 p2, https://www.isabellenhuette.com/hubfs/Files/Data-sheets/BVR.pdf

found_values.value: Answered under V288 (owner, 2026-10-01): every temperature the board reads, the onboard shunt's sensor, the motor's thermocouple and infrared channels and the ESC telemetry's temperature, each with its own limit. Applied to Onboard shunt temperature sensor as 'watched temperature'
found_values.source: Research.md V288

found_values.value: One averaged INA228 reading above SOVL trips. SLOWALERT 1, AVG 4, VSHCT and VBUSCT 1052 us, continuous shunt and bus: one averaged result each 4 x 2 x 1.052 = 8.42 ms, 8.50 ms at FOSC_TOL -1 %. ALERT asserts within 2 averaging periods, 17.0 ms, of the crossing, inside the 20 ms IOBoard.md:113 gives the ALERT. Two consecutive conversions apply to temperatures only (V288)
found_values.source: IOBoard.md:113; INA228 SLYS021A 6.5 (TCT 5h 1052 us, FOSC_TOL +/-1 %), Table 7-16 (SLOWALERT bit 13), https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/ina228.pdf

found_values.value: Detection to the main coprocessor's stop: at most 17.0 ms (V158) plus its interrupt. The ESC pack switch follows the enable node within the 500 ms stop deadline (V1), the bound the owner gives the over-temperature path under V288; the switch itself opens within 5 ms of the enable falling (F7, R3 row)
found_values.source: Research.md V1, V288, F7, R3 row; IOBoard.md:113

found_values.value: No monitor output drives the pack switch. The INA228 ALERT reaches the main coprocessor on the shared ALERT line (owner, 2026-09-30); the main coprocessor stops, and the pack switches follow the enable node alone, with no processor between GPIO6 and a gate
found_values.source: IOBoard.md:113 (Current aborts) and Link and safety (Not defeatable); Research.md R3 row

found_values.value: The INA228 accumulates both in hardware: CHARGE and ENERGY registers, energy and charge total measurement error +/-1 % at full-scale power. The specification decides the monitor's own accumulators
found_values.source: INA228 SLYS021A 6.5 (ETME), https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/ina228.pdf; IOBoard.md:454

found_values.value: 50 to 100 uOhm nominal, with the part's tolerance on top (IOBoard.md:462 decided class; V314, owner 2026-10-02). 100 uOhm +5 % = 105 uOhm gives 31.5 mV at 300 A, inside the INA228's +/-40.96 mV
found_values.source: IOBoard.md:462; Research.md V314; INA228 SLYS021A 6.5 (VDIFF ADCRANGE 1)

found_values.value: 300 A, V50's figure for the same path (owner, 2026-09-28); 'and more' carries no figure
found_values.source: Research.md V50, Scope owner decisions (Motor current)

found_values.value: A peak: 300 A for 30 s at most (V50). Budgets take the steady rise at 9 W nominal (9.45 W at +5 %), an upper bound
found_values.source: Research.md V50, V314

found_values.value: 25 mA or finer on the external path: the coarsest figure the tree states (Power.md, 25 mA on 50 uOhm, quoted in V165). The INA228 gives 0.78 mA on 100 uOhm and 1.56 mA on 50 uOhm. Applied to External shunt and Motor monitor
found_values.source: Research.md V165; IOBoard.md:463; INA228 SLYS021A 6.5 (78.125 nV LSB at ADCRANGE 1)

found_values.value: +/-1 % of reading from 15 A to 150 A onboard and to 300 A external, +/-0.15 A below 15 A (1 % of 15 A), 0 to 50 degC, after one calibration per path at 25 degC. Primary source: Tyto Robotics Flight Stand 50 datasheet V5.1 (2026-08-10), 'Current accuracy 1% from 15 to 300 A', accuracy defined as the maximum average error observed during calibration
found_values.source: https://cdn.tytorobotics.com/Documents/Datasheets/Flight-Stand-50-Datasheet.pdf (vendors.py fetch, HTTP 200), Voltage and current table and Technical definitions

found_values.value: +/-1 % of reading from 5 V to 67.2 V. Flight Stand 50 V5.1: 'Voltage accuracy 1% measured value from 5 to 180 V'
found_values.source: https://cdn.tytorobotics.com/Documents/Datasheets/Flight-Stand-50-Datasheet.pdf, Voltage and current table

found_values.value: 0 to 50 degC ambient, the owner's one range for the whole IO board (V7). Budgets take 25 K from the 25 degC calibration
found_values.source: Research.md V7

found_values.value: 4.5 W at 150 A, the larger dissipation the specification states (200 uOhm); caps the onboard shunt at 200 uOhm
found_values.source: IOBoard.md:458

found_values.value: Range 0 to at least 100 degC (V156 above); accuracy +/-2 degC, the owner's figure for the motor thermocouple channel (V235), at the 3.3 V rail
found_values.source: Research.md V235, V288, V7

found_values.value: Measure to 8.7 V, the HV port ceiling (F16), down to 0.8 V (V55); withstand 20 V, the top of the DC input (owner, 2026-09-25)
found_values.source: Research.md F16, V55, Scope owner decisions (Power)

found_values.value: 6.35 A, the rail limit one port can carry; 0.403 W in 10 mOhm
found_values.source: IOBoard.md Servo rail current row, :387

found_values.value: 10 ms plus the main coprocessor's action: the tree checks the ceiling at every sample of a 200 Hz sensor (5 ms), and the critical line must stay low for the 5 ms blanking (V287). With one INA3221 refresh of 3.63 ms max, the first conversion wholly above 3.0 A ends within 3.63 + 1.21 = 4.84 ms; 9.84 ms plus the action
found_values.source: docs/Servo.md:35; test/host/test_servo_limit.c:19 (SAMPLE_MS 5, 'a 200 Hz current sensor'); IOBoard.md:113, :389; INA3221 SBOS576C 6.5 (tCONVERT CT 100: 1.1 ms typ, 1.21 ms max), https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/ina3221.pdf

found_values.value: Yes: each INA3221's critical-alert output carries the 3.0 A ceiling to the main coprocessor on a shared line, its warning-alert output the 1.0 A stall threshold (owner, 2026-09-30); the firmware check at every sample stays on the measurement coprocessor
found_values.source: IOBoard.md:113, :387; docs/Servo.md:35-36

found_values.value: No rail monitor: one channel per port (owner, 2026-09-25) supersedes docs/Manifest.md:28's INA745A on the servo rail, as IOBoard.md's Conflicts in the tree records. The rail current is the sum of its port channels. The function takes no part
found_values.source: IOBoard.md:624; docs/Manifest.md:28

found_values.value: VBUS from the external shunt's pack-side sense lead, tapped ahead of the IN+ series resistor; the voltage is measured at the pack. The INA228's VBUS input is 0.8 to 1.2 MOhm, 0 to 85 V. Its protection is stage 2's (V306)
found_values.source: docs/Screens.md:131-134; Research.md V306; INA228 SLYS021A 6.5 (ZVBUS, VVBUS)

found_values.value: 85 V from either lead to ground and 85 V between the leads, either polarity: a lead on the wrong terminal or the load side shorted puts the pack across them; R3 clamps the pack node under 85 V. found_values.value: Thresholds: INA3221 critical 3.0 A = 30.00 mV on 10 mOhm, 750 counts of 40 uV, each conversion; warning 1.0 A = 10.00 mV, 250 counts, averaged value (AVG 4). INA228 SOVL 30.00 mV, 24,000 counts of 1.25 uV (ADCRANGE 1), both paths. Latching: INA3221 critical and warning transparent (CEN 0, WEN 0, the reset state), because the main coprocessor times the critical line against the blanking and the warning line against 400 ms; INA228 ALERT latched (ALATCH 1), cleared by a DIAG_ALRT read at re-arm only. Blanking: 5 ms, one sample of the tree's 200 Hz sensor: longer than one INA3221 refresh (3 channels, shunt only, CT 100: 3.3 ms typ, 3.63 ms max), shorter than two (6.6 ms typ); no minimum conversion time is stated. Against the port breaker: the blanking acts on 3.0 to 3.96 A only; at 3.96 to 4.84 A the port switch's breaker acts

report.figure: VBUS tap resistance on the external path
report.value: The VBUS input is 0.8 to 1.2 MOhm (ZVBUS). A series resistance R in the stage 2 VBUS protection reads the pack voltage low by R / ZVBUS: 10 kOhm gives 0.8 to 1.25 %, past V167's +/-1 % uncalibrated. Stage 2 keeps R under about 4 kOhm (0.5 %) or the calibration covers it

INA3221 critical 30.00 mV (3.0 A on 10 mOhm, 750 counts of 40 uV, each conversion); warning 10.00 mV (1.0 A, 250 counts, averaged, AVG 4); INA228 SOVL 30.00 mV (24,000 counts of 1.25 uV, ADCRANGE 1) on both paths: 150 A x 200 uOhm and 300 A x 100 uOhm. With the shunts at their upper tolerance the trips fall to 148.5 A (BVR +1 %) and 285.7 A (BAS +5 %)

INA3221 critical and warning transparent (CEN 0, WEN 0, the reset state): the main coprocessor times the lines (5 ms blanking, 400 ms stall) and cannot clear a latch, which only a Mask/Enable read on the measurement coprocessor's bus clears. INA228 ALERT latched (ALATCH 1), cleared by a DIAG_ALRT read at re-arm only; with ALATCH 1 any DIAG_ALRT read clears it, so the firmware does not poll DIAG_ALRT for CNVRF while armed

5 ms, one sample of the tree's 200 Hz current sensor. One INA3221 refresh (3 channels, shunt only, CT 100) is 3.3 ms typ, 3.63 ms max: a single conversion above 3.0 A holds its node low for at most 3.63 ms and is logged; two consecutive conversions hold it 6.6 ms typ and abort. The INA3221 states no minimum conversion time, so the shortest two-conversion pulse is not stated. The 7th part keeps all 3 channels enabled so its refresh matches. Two parts' single trips that overlap on the shared line can exceed 5 ms together; the shift register names them

The critical threshold acts between 2.95 and 3.05 A (INA3221 26.2 mA plus ERJ-6CWDR010V 22.9 mA). The blanking covers 3.0 to 3.96 A only; from 3.96 to 4.84 A the port switch's breaker acts. The band is the owner's figure (IOBoard.md:113); R6's Port supply switch has no part in selection.json, and V312 names TLP3545A with an INA301A1IDGKR trip on the same port shunt, so the band rests on parts not yet verified

INA3221 critical and warning limits reset to 7FF8h (positive full scale, alerts in effect off), CEN and WEN 0; INA228 SOVL resets to 7FFFh and ALATCH to 0 (transparent). No alert carries an abort until the measurement coprocessor writes the limits, as IOBoard.md:113 requires before arming

INA3221 refresh 3.63 ms max a channel (shunt only, CT 100); a port above 3.0 A reaches the first conversion wholly above it within 4.84 ms, plus 5 ms blanking: 9.84 ms plus the main coprocessor's action (V173). 7 parts on two buses, 4 and 3, 21 channels, 0x40 to 0x43 on each bus

49.1 mA of the owner's +/-50 mA at 3.0 A, uncalibrated, 0 to 50 degC: INA3221 26.2 mA plus ERJ-6CWDR010V 22.9 mA, margin 0.9 mA. The ERJ figure rests on a 9.9 K self-heating derived from the derating curve; the sheet states no thermal resistance. Noise: about one 40 uV LSB (4 mA) typical at 1.1 ms in Figure 7-7, no maximum stated, against 20 mA peak-to-peak
report.source: SBOS576C 6.5, Figure 7-7; AOA0000C313 ratings and derating; Research.md V174

found_values.value: 1.69 A into a full pack at 8.4 V from a 3.0 A source: 15 W x 94.7 % (V139) = 14.2 W, / 8.4 V; 1.58 A at the 2,800 mA lower edge of the 2.9 A input setting (0x3A00H); 2.01 to 2.15 A into the 6.6 V floor of V294 (computed). Below VSYS_MIN for 2S the charge is clamped at 384 mA

found_values.value: 3000 mAh for the 2S1P pack, so 3000 mAh a cell ('Kapazität: 3000mAh'). No source states a minimum capacity or run time. found_values.value: Charge: fast charge from 10 °C ('minimal 10°C') to 40 °C ('max. 40°C'); under 10 °C below 1C, typically 0.2C to 0.5C; V311 sets no charge below 10 °C. Discharge: never above 60 °C; below 18 °C loads above 5C need preheating (V296 holds 15 A or less); near 10 °C under 50 % of the usual C rate. The board ambient is 0 to 50 °C (V7) and the owner's pack limits 0 to 55 °C (V150)
found_values.source: https://www.stefansliposhop.de/media/general/LiPoFAQV15c.pdf sections 'Laden wenn der LiPo sehr kalt oder warm ist', 'Und wenn es mal kalt (unter 18°C) wird?'; Research.md V7, V150, V296, V311 at 68adf31

found_values.value: The RP2354B's USB port: one USB Type-C connector carries the F8 charger input, the RP2354B's D+ and D-, and CC1 and CC2, VBUS rated 5.5 V at 3 A. It has no SuperSpeed pair, so the Default current is 500 mA (USB 2.0)
found_values.source: hardware/docs/Research.md V10 and V13 answers (owner, 2026-09-28) at checkout 68adf31bf1c74e2a2c1f32ba925b462a9696115f

found_values.value: On the IO board, as an LCSC part JLCPCB places: 'SLS Akkus verfügen über keine eigene Schutzschaltung', so the pack as sold has no protection, and its XH balance lead reaches the board
found_values.source: https://www.stefansliposhop.de/media/general/SLS_Sicherheitshinweise_DE_A4.pdf section 2; IOBoard.md Pack overcurrent protection at 68adf31

found_values.value: Owner: over-temperature 55 °C and under-temperature 0 °C (2026-09-30), and no charge below 10 °C (V311). Found: per-cell overvoltage on charge at 4.25 V, 50 mV above the maker's 4.2 V full charge and above the BQ25723's 8.4 V upper edge of 4.2252 V a cell. Short circuit: a band above the overcurrent band and at or below the pack's 60C (180 A) burst, whose duration the vendor does not state: SCD1 88.8 mV on 1 mOhm +-0.5 % gives 77.03 to 100.68 A untrimmed
found_values.source: https://www.stefansliposhop.de/media/general/SLS_Sicherheitshinweise_DE_A4.pdf section 3; https://www.stefansliposhop.de/akkus/sls-xtron/sls-xtron-30c/sls-xtron-3000mah-2s1p-7-4v-30c-60c::1031.html 'Kurzzeitiger Entladestrom: max. 60C (180,0A)'; bq25723.pdf SLUSE64 8.5; bq40z80.pdf SLUSBV4D 5.5

found_values.value: Yes, up to the 3.0 A input limit at 5 V (15 W) less the charge current. The BQ25723's NVDC path regulates VSYS at VSYS_MIN, 6.6 V for 2S (Table 9-2): 'Even with a depleted battery, the system is regulated above the minimum system voltage' (9.4.1.1). The servo converters' draw far exceeds 15 W, so firmware keeps them off on USB-C alone
found_values.source: https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/bq25723.pdf SLUSE64 Table 9-2, 9.4.1.1

found_values.value: Yes: USB-C is the only charge source (F8), so a pack at the floor recovers on the bench only by charging while the floor disconnect holds discharge off. With the BQ40Z80 as the one protector, CUV sets XDSG only, charging stays allowed, and with Protection Configuration[CUV_RECOV_CHG] = 1 the CUV recovers only with charging present and every cell at or above CUV:Recovery. The charger connects on the pack side of the protector's FETs
found_values.source: https://www.ti.com/lit/pdf/sluubt5 SLUUBT5C 3.2 Cell Undervoltage Protection (vendors.py fetch, HTTP 200, 4,683,293 bytes); F8 answer

found_values.value: 8.4 V nominal full charge (4.2 V a cell): the maker's safety notes state 'Voll geladen ... 4,2 V pro Zelle' (section 3). R5 designs the pack path to 8.45 V, with the charger's regulation tolerance on top
found_values.source: https://www.stefansliposhop.de/media/general/SLS_Sicherheitshinweise_DE_A4.pdf REV.1.06 section 3

found_values.value: The USB-C charger present (charging detected), and then every cell at or above the V94 release. The load returning alone never reconnects the pack, and the DC input does not, since it never charges the pack (F8). An operator wake contact restarts the IC from the pack alone (V301); a cell under the trip trips it again
found_values.source: IOBoard.md Pack disconnect hysteresis row; F8 and V301 Answers

found_values.value: 3.75 V a cell, the maker's lowest voltage at rest ('Im Ruhezustand sollte die Spannung pro Zelle nicht unter 3,75 V fallen'); its guide gives 3.70 V. 0.45 V above the 3.3 V floor under load
found_values.source: https://www.stefansliposhop.de/media/general/SLS_Sicherheitshinweise_DE_A4.pdf REV.1.06 section 4; https://www.stefansliposhop.de/media/general/LiPoFAQV15c.pdf 'Zusammenfassend'

found_values.value: Answered by V295: 3.3 V a cell under load is the lowest trip at every corner; the threshold sits above it by the IC's band. BQ40Z80RSMR: +/-83 mV at 3.3 V (K +/-1 %, gain error 0.8 % of FSR with FSR = VFS 1.225 V, offset 157 uV / K), or +/-132 mV if FSR spans -VFS to +VFS; threshold 3,383 mV or 3,432 mV. The figures hold over -40 to 85 degC; none bounds 0 to 50 degC alone
found_values.source: Research.md V294, V295; https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/bq40z80.pdf SLUSBV4D 5.5

found_values.value: No source sets a lower bound. The maker forbids a cell under 3.3 V under load 'auch nicht kurzzeitig' (not even briefly), so the filter has an upper bound: the cell must not fall from the threshold to 3.3 V within it. That fall rate is not known (internal resistance not measured, V285). Taken: the shortest delay the IC allows, stated with its granularity
found_values.source: https://www.stefansliposhop.de/media/general/LiPoFAQV15c.pdf 'Zusammenfassend'; Research.md V285

found_values.value: 10 uA at most from the pack while it is disconnected, with an operator wake contact for a start from the pack alone (V301)
found_values.source: Research.md V301 Answer

found_values.value: (b): the pack protection R7 selects, one IC for the disconnect, the overcurrent protection, the balance lead and the pack temperature (V297, V298), its threshold in the IC nonvolatile memory, written once before the board ships. Not (c): a threshold firmware writes at each start-up is not in force before the write
found_values.source: Research.md V297, V298 Answers and the Power decision of 2026-09-24

found_values.value: 25 % on each rail, chosen: each rail part is rated at least 1.25 times its summed load. 3.3 V: 1,475 mA x 1.25 = 1.84 A. 5 V: 2.08 A x 1.25 = 2.60 A. It covers the R6, R7 and R8 parts not in the sum and loads stated as typical only
found_values.source: round1/FU-B3/002-P2-R5.json V99 (chosen value, confirmed by FU-B1, FU-2B1 and FU-2F P4); report 3.3 V and 5 V rail load

found_values.value: +/-5 %, 4.75 V to 5.25 V. The load-cell excitation runs from R13 own regulator (V254) and the encoder 5 V from the encoder converter (V108), so neither is on the 5 V rail; the board own 5 V load is the TCAN1472VDRQ1 (VCC 4.5 to 5.5 V); the encoder 5 V position takes 5 VDC +/-5 % (E6B2-CWZ1X)
found_values.source: https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tcan1472-q1.pdf recommended VCC; https://www.ia.omron.com/products/family/487/specification.html power supply voltage row; round1/FU-C1/004-P2-R13.json V254

found_values.value: 345 Ohm: 350 +/- 5 Ohm input resistance of each cell (TAS501). Three cells at 5.25 V draw 45.7 mA from R13 own regulator, not from the 5 V rail
found_values.source: https://cdn.sparkfun.com/assets/parts/1/2/2/3/8/TAS501.pdf input resistance row

found_values.value: Steady: 100 mA at 12 V (E6B2-CWZ5B 0.8 W, 100 mA max) and 160 mA at 5 V (E6B2-CWZ1X); the current consumption row carries note *1, the power-on inrush (about 9 A for about 0.3 ms in FU-2F reading of the note). No encoder is named in the tree; the Omron E6B2-C series is the class taken
found_values.source: https://www.ia.omron.com/products/family/487/specification.html current consumption row

found_values.value: 10.8 V to 13.2 V at the encoder connector: 12 VDC -10 % is the E6B2-CWZ5B lowest; 12 VDC +10 % the E6B2-CWZ3E highest
found_values.source: https://www.ia.omron.com/products/family/487/specification.html power supply voltage row

found_values.value: No: 'Every bus is one signal wire plus ground into a coprocessor pin' (docs/Receivers.md:15); the SILENT state sends the operator to 'receiver power, wiring, pin' (:29). No rail, voltage or current is assigned
found_values.source: docs/Receivers.md at checkout 68adf31bf1c7

found_values.value: 25.2 A at 12 V and 15.2 A at 20 V (302.0 W in, as V90), and 31.1 A at 9.73 V, the lowest falling corner of V88, where the DC input still runs the board. R5 sizes the DC path for 25.2 A continuous and 31.1 A at the handover corner
found_values.source: V90, V88 found; IOBoard.md DC input row; arithmetic

found_values.value: Either order. The one IO board part on both rails is the TCAN1472VDRQ1 (VCC 5 V, VIO 3.3 V), with undervoltage protection on both supplies and passive behaviour unpowered; the 5 V rail feeds the display through the TPS25947, which blocks reverse current
found_values.source: https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tcan1472-q1.pdf features, UVCC, UVIO; https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tps25947.pdf 7.3.7

found_values.value: Yes, required: with the pack power leads connected and its balance lead unplugged or one wire open, the disconnect holds the pack off, with and without a charger. V301: the behaviour may rest on the IC undervoltage logic, an inference; a bench test (mid wire open, with and without a charger, and first cell attach) confirms it before the pages call V107 met
found_values.source: Research.md V301 Answer; F9 Answer

found_values.value: 250 mA nominal, 233 to 267 mA: the encoder converter own output current limit in both F4 jumper positions (VSNS 28 / 30 / 32 mV at IOUT_LIMIT 10111100b over 120 mOhm), above the encoder steady 160 mA and 100 mA; a short on the encoder cable leaves the 5 V rail and the display supply untouched
found_values.source: https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tps55288.pdf SLVSF01B 6.5 VSNS

found_values.value: Cut-off state: yes, through the port monitor's bus-voltage reading, which falls behind an open switch (an inference; no line states it); with V130 the firmware reports the cut-off. Jumper position: no; the setup screen lists the ceilings as 'each set in hardware'

found_values.value: 20 V: the TPS55285 programs up to 15 V, its output OVP trips at 110.5 to 120 % of the target, VOUT is rated 17 V absolute maximum, and a converter failed through passes the DC input, 20 V at most
found_values.source: SLVSI72A, ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tps55285.pdf, read 2026-10-02T20:21:39Z 5.1, 5.2, 5.4

found_values.value: Each port switch switches its port from 0.8 V (V55) to 8.4 V, on and carrying the port's current from 0.8 V (V282); the function may be split across parts (V302); the switch conducts both ways while on and blocks the pin up to 12 V while off, with no reverse-blocking part (V126, V312). The TPS259474LRPWR takes VIN only from 2.7 V (IOBoard.md Port supply switch, SLVSFC9C)
found_values.source: Research.md@68adf31 V126, V277, V282, V302, V312; IOBoard.md@68adf31 Port supply switch

found_values.value: 3.72 A: the continuous output current one TPS55285 holds at 6.0 V in, 8.4 V out and 50 degC with the junction at the 125 degC recommended maximum on V281's 33 degC/W (loss budget 2.27 W), every converter loss of V111's model counted in the IC. 3.94 A with the SRP1265A-4R7M's 8.4 mOhm maximum DC loss taken out of the IC's budget; 4.11 A with 14.3 mOhm taken out. Typical 25 degC curves; RDS(on) rise with temperature not stated and not counted; heatsink not credited. At the V294 floor of 6.6 V: 4.12 A (4.36 A less 8.4 mOhm)
found_values.source: SLVSI72A, ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tps55285.pdf, read 2026-10-02T20:21:39Z 5.2 (TJ 125 degC), 5.3 (RthJA 33 degC/W, EVM), Figure 5-3; Research.md@68adf31 V281; scratch/FU-2H/P2-R6/thermal3.py output 'VIN 6.0 VOUT 8.4: all-loss (3.72, 5.59, 2.27, 93.2)' and t4.py (2026-10-02T20:43Z)

found_values.value: Each port is cut off above 6.0 V (LV) or 8.7 V (HV), set by a jumper (F16), within V128's bands; the port reconnects by itself once the rail falls below the ceiling with the comparator's own hysteresis, no latch, and the firmware reports the cut-off (V130)
found_values.source: Research.md@68adf31 V128, V130, V280, F16; IOBoard.md@68adf31 Port voltage ceiling

found_values.value: The TPS55285 takes current back into its output and passes it to its input in FPWM only: 'The high-side N-MOSFET is not turned off even if the current through the MOSFET is zero. Thus, the inductor current changes its direction after it runs to zero. The power flow is from output side to input side' (6.4.1). In PFM, the default (MODE register 06h bit 1 = 0), it turns the switches off at zero current 'to prevent the reverse current from output to input' (6.4.2), so a returned current raises the rail. No reverse or negative current limit is stated in the data sheet. Input OVP, 22.0 to 23.0 V rising, stops switching when the input cannot sink the returned current (6.3.14). Output OVP at 110.5 to 120 % of the target (9.28 to 10.08 V at 8.4 V; 6.08 to 6.6 V at 5.5 V) lies above both ceilings. The energy a servo returns is not stated on the servo pages read (Savox SH-0255MG+, SB-2290SG): not known
found_values.source: SLVSI72A, ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tps55285.pdf, read 2026-10-02T20:21:39Z 5.4, 6.3.14, 6.3.15, 6.4.1, 6.4.2, 7.6; Savox pages (vendors.py fetch 20:36:05Z, 20:36:06Z)

figures.evidence: The premise 'the two shunt paths replace each other, so one INA228 answers per test' does not follow. IOBoard.md:442 says a test is cabled through one path, but IOBoard.md:503 puts two INA228 on one bus with no switch in a sense path, and a powered INA228 acknowledges its address whatever its IN+/IN-/VBUS are wired to (SLYS021A 7.5.1, Table 7-2). Both answer every test, so 'the monitor whenever it answers' cannot pick the cabled one. The value also says the selector is not stated, yet the tree has one: the ina228_en and one-address ina228_addr settings (shared/settings/settings.c:27-29, :85-95; IOBoard.md:503 'takes one address'). The telemetry-only source on the bring-up module is confirmed (firmware/iomcu/src/main.c:714-725; docs/OpenYGE.md:380-381).

Thresholds and latching re-derive (see the thresholds and latching entries). The blanking claim does not hold from the datasheet: INA3221 7.3.2.1 says the Critical alert pin 'pulls low if any channel measurement exceeds the limit' on 'individual conversions of each channel' and states nothing on when the pin releases in transparent mode (CEN 0, Table 8-34). The value takes a single over-limit conversion to hold the pin low for at most 3.63 ms and two consecutive ones for 6.6 ms typ, which assumes the pin is held until the same channel converts again. If the pin follows each conversion, a sustained overcurrent on one channel of a three-channel part pulls it low for about one conversion in three (1.1 ms typ, 1.21 ms max), never above the 5 ms blanking, and the port abort never fires. Figure 9-2 shows one channel only. tCONVERT has no minimum, which the value states.

figures.evidence: IOBoard.md:624 follows one monitor channel per port; docs/Manifest.md:28 lists INA745A on the servo rail and is superseded. The function takes no part.

Checked against IOBoard.md:74, :453-454, :463-464, :503, the answers V177, V288, V304, and the found values V154, V155, V158 to V161, V165 to V168, V287 whose rows name the Motor monitor. Every requirement is in the list: fixed part, high-side bus and input rating, trip inside full scale, SOVL, latch, 20 ms, alert output, current and voltage accuracy, resolution, charge and energy, reading, addresses, 0 to 50 degC. No value is weaker than its source; the 25 degC calibration in the current accuracy is the found V166's disclosed condition. V179's 85 V fault and V306 sit under External shunt sense input, whose row does not name the Motor monitor. V288's temperatures exclude the INA228 die temperature.

requirements.name: overcurrent threshold

requirements.name: charge overvoltage
requirements.required: per-cell overvoltage on charge settable to 4.25 V (V150)

requirements.name: undervoltage trip
requirements.required: lowest trip 3.3 V a cell under load, threshold above it by the IC's accuracy band (V294, V295)

requirements.name: undervoltage release
requirements.required: released only with charging present and every cell above a recovery voltage (V93, V297)

requirements.name: threshold in non-volatile memory

requirements.datasheet: thresholds in data flash; the 2S cell configuration is written before first use

requirements.name: temperature

requirements.datasheet: OTC (default 55.0 C), OTD (60.0 C), UTC, UTD thresholds -40.0 to 150.0 C in 0.1 C; UTC acts when charging above Chg Current Threshold (50 mA default) after UTC:Delay 0 to 255 s and sets XCHG; UTC settable to 10.0 C

requirements.name: NTC

requirements.name: FET drive at the floor

data.ruling: The stock verifier's refutation holds, so the refutation stands. INA228AIDGSR fails sourcing rule 4 at JLCPCB. The exact LCSC match C2887910 reads stockCount 0 and canPresaleNumber -236. The need is 5 boards (S7) x 2 placements (IOBoard.md:74, :112, :465 and :503, one INA228 for each shunt path) = 10. S4 sets the gate at 5 x 10 = 50, never under 50, so the gate is 50, and 0 is under it. Rule 4 also fails any negative presale count, whatever the stock says. The part is not held: neither the Held parts table nor inventory-2026-09-25.csv has an INA2xx row, so rule 6 does not apply. The rule 5 second-vendor route fails as well. Digi-Key reads 0 in all three packagings, with a manufacturer lead time of 20 weeks. The datasheet verifier confirmed every check and refuted nothing. The stock verifier's other checks pass and are not part of the refutation: lifecycle ACTIVE at TI and Active at Digi-Key, no end-of-life notice, LCSC identity, library type expand, and Texas Instruments is on the S1 allowlist. The owner's answer to V304 (2026-10-02) keeps INA228AIDGSR fixed. It records the unmet gate as a current limitation and gives it to T6 as a stock exception, with the stock read again before the order. Under Scope, Fixed inputs, a fixed input that fails a check is reported to the owner and is not re-selected. V304 therefore does not make rule 4 pass. The refutation stands, the part stays the owner's fixed input, and no replacement candidate goes to new verifiers. Scope is function, because the failure is the rule 4 quantity gate and not one of the part-level causes (lifecycle, end-of-life notice, allowlist, LCSC identity). With stock 0 and a negative presale count, the gate also fails at the 1 placement of External shunt sense input. Earlier adjudicators split on this scope: FU-2B2/015 and FU-2G/010 ruled part, FU-2G/011 ruled function. This ruling agrees with FU-2B2/015 and FU-2G/010 on stands.

data.ruling: The refutation stands. The value's step "the two shunt paths replace each other, so one INA228 answers per test" does not follow from its sources. The owner's rule (IOBoard.md:442) is that a test is cabled through one shunt path, never both. It says nothing about which monitor is on the bus. Under F1 (owner, 2026-09-25) and IOBoard.md:503, the board carries two INA228s, one for each path, with no switch in a sense path. Each has its own A0/A1 address on the measurement coprocessor's I2C bus. The INA228 datasheet makes the address acknowledge depend only on the A0/A1 pin states and a valid address byte, not on what IN+, IN- or VBUS are wired to. So both powered INA228s answer in every test, and the rule "the monitor whenever it answers" cannot pick the cabled path. That makes the value incomplete as a rule for filling BENCH page 0x20 registers 0 and 1. A secondary point: the tree already has a selector, a single ina228_en setting and a one-address ina228_addr setting (0x40, 0x41, 0x44 or 0x45). IOBoard.md:503 says that setting "takes one address". So "how the firmware tells which path is cabled is not stated" overlooks the configured address. The confirmed parts of the value still hold: on the bring-up module the ESC telemetry is the only voltage and current source (main.c), and the ESC's figures and the shunt are independent measurements (OpenYGE.md:380-381). The finding is about this function's requirement value (V154, Motor monitor), not about the INA228 part, so its scope is function.
data.evidence: Datasheet SLYS021A (Rev. A, May 2022), 7.5.1: "The device has two address pins, A0 and A1. Table 7-2 lists the pin logic levels for each of the 16 possible addresses. The device samples the state of pins A0 and A1 on every bus communication." 7.5.1.1: "This byte is the secondary device address, with the R/W bit low. The device then acknowledges receipt of a valid address." Neither section makes the acknowledge depend on the shunt or bus inputs. Checkout 68adf31: hardware/docs/IOBoard.md:442: "The two paths replace each other: a test is cabled through one of them, never both (owner, 2026-09-25)." IOBoard.md:503 (Motor monitor address): "two INA228, one for each shunt path (F1), each set by its A0 and A1 pins to its own address. The display's INA228 address setting offers 0x40, 0x41, 0x44 and 0x45 and takes one address". Research.md:678, F1, owner's answer: "one INA238 for each path (owner, 2026-09-25)"; the proposed answer there reads "no switch sits in a sense path, and the firmware reads whichever is wired. The two positions differ by I2C address". Research.md:707 applies V154 to the INA228. shared/settings/settings.c:29 has k_ina_addr = {"0x40","0x41","0x44","0x45"}. settings.c:87-95 defines SET_INA228_EN ("ina228_en"), SET_INA228_ADDR ("ina228_addr", "Set by its A0 and A1 pins", one enum value) and SET_INA228_SHUNT. firmware/iomcu/src/main.c:714-727 has the comment "There is no other source for any of these on this board" and fills voltage and current only from extended DShot telemetry (EDT).

missed.why: A family P2 did not consider (INA381A1 to A4, comparator reference set on a pin, not by a limit resistor as on the INA301). Every requirement value passes. Data sheet SBOS848B (https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/ina381.pdf, read 2026-10-02T21:10:27Z): common-mode input -0.2 to 26 V (covers 0.8 to 8.70 V, 12 V back-fed while off, 20 V through a failed converter; differential absolute maximum +/-26 V, so a braking servo's negative VSENSE drives the output to GND without damage and without a trip); supply 2.7 to 5.5 V (3.201 to 3.399 V passes); A1 gain 20 V/V, gain error 1 % max, offset 150 uV max at VCM 0 V and 500 uV max at VCM 12 V, comparator offset 5 mV max, hysteresis 50 mV; open-drain active-low ALERT (6 V absolute maximum) that pulls the TPSI3052 EN low; latch mode with RESET high, cleared when RESET is pulled low for at least 100 ns, so RESET goes to the port's enable and the trip holds the switch off while the enable is high; response: comparator alone 0.4 us typ / 1 us max, total small-signal alert 2 us typ / 5 us max, slew-limited alert 3 us typ / 10 us max (reported, V129 states no limit). Trip band on the 10 mOhm port shunt (assumed +/-0.8 % with temperature coefficient) with CMPREF 0.88 V: 4.11 to 4.70 A when CMPREF is a 0.1 % divider off the 3.201 to 3.399 V rail, 4.23 to 4.58 A from the 1.25 V REF3112 (my arithmetic, worst case, 25 K from 25 degC): inside 3.0 to 6.35 A and inside the 3.96 to 4.84 A breaker band. Stock: JLCPCB C544574 stockCount 615, canPresaleNumber 539, expand, USD 0.387 at 500 (vendors.py jlcpcb, 2026-10-02T21:11:23Z), passes the gate of 500 (20 placements x 5 boards x 5) by 115. Digi-Key INA381A1IDSGR Active, stock 8602, lead 20 weeks (productdetails, 2026-10-02T21:12:09Z), so rule 5 passes by the second vendor. TI page https://www.ti.com/product/INA381 reads ACTIVE (2026-10-02T21:24:30Z); first data sheet December 2017. WSON-8 2 x 2 mm, thermal pad to GND. Same-footprint sibling INA381A2IDSGR (gain 50, CMPREF 2.2 V): JLCPCB C2155688 4774/4538 (21:11:22Z) but Digi-Key stock 0 (21:12:08Z), so it is not a second source of its own and needs another divider. INA301A1IDGKR's JLCPCB price is USD 1.76 at 500 (jlcparts), about four times this part's.

data.ruling: The refutation stands for the blanking part of V287's value. The thresholds (750 counts of 40 uV, 250 counts, INA228 24,000 counts of 1.25 uV) and the latching settings (CEN 0 and WEN 0, which are the reset state) re-derive, and the verifier does not dispute them. The 5 ms blanking does not hold from the maker's datasheet. Its margins are "longer than one INA3221 refresh (3.3 ms typ, 3.63 ms max), shorter than two (6.6 ms typ)". Both assume that in transparent mode an over-limit conversion holds the Critical pin low until the same channel converts again. SBOS576C does not state this. Section 7.3.2.1 says only that the pin "pulls low if any channel measurement exceeds the limit". Table 8-34 defines CEN 0 only as "Transparent (default)". Section 9.2 and Figure 9-2 show one enabled channel, "Enabled channel CH1", so they cannot show how three channels share the pin. Nothing in the datasheet rules out the verifier's case. There, the pin follows each conversion of any channel. A sustained overcurrent on one of three shunt-only channels would then hold the pin low for 1.1 ms typ, 1.21 ms max, in every 3.3 ms cycle. That never exceeds 5 ms, so the 3.0 A abort never fires. Secondary sources, which are not the maker's datasheet, leave the question open. On TI E2E thread 807608, a TI engineer says a transparent pin "should restore automatically after one conversion", without saying which channel's conversion. In the same thread a user measured the Ch.1 critical pin "active for 50ms (6 channels sampled x 8.24ms)", which fits the hold-until-same-channel model, but the post does not state the alert mode. On thread 1625525, a TI engineer says the transparent alert "clears as soon as the shunt voltage drops back down below the programmed level", without a multi-channel case. The pin's release timing with three channels enabled is therefore not read from any maker document, and the value presents a blanking margin that rests on it. Under the page's rules that figure is written as not read, not derived. Scope is function: the finding concerns V287's blanking requirement for the Port current monitor and its configuration, not the INA3221's lifecycle or identity.
data.evidence: SBOS576C (revised September 2026), 7.3.2.1: "The Critical alert pin pulls low if any channel measurement exceeds the limit present in the corresponding-channel critical-alert limit register." No sentence states when the pin releases. Table 8-34: bit 10 CEN "Critical alert latch enable ... 0 = Transparent (default), 1 = Latch enabled"; CF1-3 "cleared when the Mask/Enable register is read back"; nothing on pin release. 7.4.2.1: with shunt only on 3 channels, "two conversions" pass before the device converts the same channel again. 6.5 tCONVERT CT=100: 1.1 ms typ, 1.21 ms max, no minimum. 9.2.1 Table 9-1: "Enabled channel CH1"; Figure 9-2 shows a single channel at 1.1 ms. A full-text search of the datasheet for until/clears/release/deassert finds no release condition for the Critical or Warning pin in transparent mode. The only "until the interrupt is cleared" is in 7.5.3, SMBus alert response, which requires Latch mode. TI E2E 807608, TI engineer: "If the Critical pin is set to transparent mode, after the over limit condition is removed, the Critical pin should restore automatically after one conversion." The same thread's user: "The Critical flag (Ch.1) remains active for 50ms (6 channels sampled x 8.24ms)", alert mode not stated. TI E2E 1625525, TI engineer: transparent alerts "actively change state with the signal ... As soon as the shunt voltage drops back down below the programmed level, the alert clears." Neither TI statement addresses three enabled channels.

data.function: P2 report: Critical line blanking time (V287)
data.ruling: The refutation holds. The refresh figures re-derive. tCONVERT at CT=100 is 1.1 ms typical and 1.21 ms maximum (6.5). Three shunt-only channels give one refresh of 3.3 ms typical and 3.63 ms maximum (7.4.1). SBOS576C gives no minimum conversion time. The hold times the claim builds on these figures do not come from the datasheet. "A single conversion holds its node low for at most 3.63 ms; two consecutive hold it 6.6 ms typ and abort" assumes that the transparent Critical pin stays low from one over-limit conversion of a channel until that same channel's next conversion. It also assumes that the in-limit conversions of the other two channels in between do not release the pin. SBOS576C does not say this. 7.3.2.1 says only that the pin "pulls low if any channel measurement exceeds the limit". Table 8-34 defines CEN=0 only as "Transparent (default)". 9.2.2 and Figure 9-2 show one enabled channel (CH1) and say only that the pin "pulls low after the conversion cycle completes". With three channels enabled, the release point is not stated. The two TI E2E threads (Engineer-to-Engineer, TI's support forum) do not settle it either. In thread 1625525, a TI engineer says the transparent alert "clears" as soon as the shunt voltage drops below the limit. He says nothing about another channel's conversion. In thread 807608, a customer saw Ch.1's critical alert stay active for 50 ms = 6 channels x 8.24 ms, which fits the claim's model. That is one unqualified scope observation, under unstated conditions while he raised the limit, not a maker figure. A TI engineer there says the pin restores "after one conversion", without naming which channel's. Under the verifier's reading, a sustained overcurrent on one channel holds the shared line low for about 1.1 ms in every 3.3 ms. That stays below the 5 ms blanking at every current, so the abort would never fire. The datasheet does not rule that reading out. The figure states an unknown as a fact. It holds only after a bench measurement of the Critical pin with 3 channels enabled and one over the limit, or after TI states the release point. Scope is function: the point is the blanking time's fit to this function's alert timing, not the part's identity or lifecycle.
data.evidence: SBOS576C (revised September 2026), 6.5: tCONVERT at CT bit = 100 is 1.1 ms typical, 1.21 ms maximum; no minimum. 7.4.1: one sequence's time is the sum of the enabled conversion times; 3 shunt-only channels give 3.3 ms typical, 3.63 ms maximum. 7.3.2.1: "The Critical alert pin pulls low if any channel measurement exceeds the limit present in the corresponding-channel critical-alert limit register"; nothing on when it releases. Table 8-34, bit 10 CEN: "0 = Transparent (default) / 1 = Latch enabled"; transparent behaviour not defined further. 9.2.2 and Figure 9-2: one enabled channel (CH1); the pin "pulls low after the conversion cycle completes". E2E 1625525, TI engineer: in transparent mode "As soon as the shunt voltage drops back down below the programmed level, the alert clears" (per signal; other channels not mentioned). E2E 807608, customer: "The Critical flag (Ch.1) remains active for 50ms (6 channels sampled x 8.24ms)"; TI engineer: "the Critical pin should restore automatically after one conversion" (which channel's conversion not stated). The datasheet states no release point with 3 channels enabled. The hold times 3.63 ms max and 6.6 ms typ are an inference. Not measured.

data.ruling: The refutation holds. The claim gives its source as SLUSBV4D 5.5. That table lists a maximum tSCD1 of 1850 us with PROTECTION_CONTROL[SCDDx2] = 1, so the claimed "1830 us with SCDDx2" does not match it. 1830 us is the 0x0F entry of SLUUBT5C Table A-10, which is the technical reference manual (TRM), not the cited source. The two TI documents differ by 20 us. The rest of the figure reproduces from the sources. SCD1 88.8 mV is Table A-8 setting 0x02 (RSNS = 1). The 1 mOhm +-0.5 % shunt with -10/+10 % scale error untrimmed gives 77.03 to 100.68 A: (79.92 - 2.5) / 1.005 and (97.68 + 2.5) / 0.995. The ±5 % scale error and ±2.5 mV offset post-trim give 81.45 to 96.22 A. The delay without SCDDx2 is 0 to 915 us. Only the SCDDx2 delay is wrong for the cited source. A corrected figure reads "0 to 1850 us (SLUSBV4D 5.5); largest setting 1830 us (SLUUBT5C Table A-10, 0x0F)". The ruling concerns this figure's value and source in this function, not the part's identity or lifecycle.
data.evidence: SLUSBV4D (June 2018, revised May 2026) section 5.5, Current Protection Timing: tSCD1 is 0 to 915 us with PROTECTION_CONTROL[SCDDx2] = 0 and 0 to 1850 us with SCDDx2 = 1. The program step ΔtSCD1 is 61 us and 121 us. VSCD1 with RSNS = 1 is -44.4 to -200 mV in 22.2 mV steps. VSCALE is -10 % to 10 % untrimmed and -5 % to 5 % post-trim. VOFFSET is -2.5 to 2.5 mV post-trim. SLUUBT5C Table A-8 lists 0x02 as -88.8 mV (RSNS = 1). Table A-9 (SCDDx2 = 0) runs 0x0F = 915 us. Table A-10 (SCDDx2 = 1) runs 0x0F = 1830 us.

requirements.name: one IC on the pack
requirements.required: disconnect, overcurrent, balance lead and temperature in one IC
requirements.datasheet: pack manager with voltage, current and temperature protection, high-side N-channel FET drive, cell voltage on VC1 to VC4, thermistor inputs TS1 to TS4

requirements.name: lowest trip
requirements.required: 3.3 V a cell at every corner, band stated
requirements.datasheet: CUV:Threshold 0 to 32767 mV in data flash; cell scaling K 0.1980 / 0.2000 / 0.2020 (7.10), ADC gain error +/-0.8 % of FSR, offset +/-157 uV multiplied by 1/K (7.16): the same +/-83 mV at 3.3 V (+/-132 mV if FSR spans -VFS to VFS) as the BQ40Z80, so a threshold of 3,432 mV covers both; minimum and maximum over -40 to 85 degC

requirements.name: cells
requirements.datasheet: 1-series to 4-series Li-ion or Li-polymer

requirements.name: reconnect condition
requirements.required: charger present and every cell >= release
requirements.datasheet: Protection Configuration[CUV_RECOV_CHG] = 1: recovery needs min cell voltage >= CUV:Recovery AND charging detected (BatteryStatus()[DSG] = 0)

requirements.name: release voltage
requirements.datasheet: CUV:Recovery 0 to 32767 mV (I2), set 3750 mV

requirements.name: trip filter
requirements.datasheet: CUV:Delay 0 to 255 s (U1), 1 s granularity, set 0 s; the averaging note of the BQ40Z80 TRM (setting plus up to 1.5 s) is not in this TRM: not stated here

requirements.name: current while disconnected
requirements.datasheet: voltage-based SHUTDOWN (5.4.1) with CHG and DSG off: ISHUTDOWN 1.6 uA typical, no maximum stated; VC input leakage 1 uA maximum each (7.10); a 1 MOhm mid-cell pull-down adds up to 4.2 uA: about 7.6 uA by the BQ40Z80 sum. Passes on the typical figure only

requirements.name: threshold set in hardware
requirements.datasheet: protections and thresholds in data flash; written over SMBus

requirements.name: balance lead open
requirements.required: held off with and without charger
requirements.datasheet: the permanent failure OPNCELL compares BAT with the sum of the cells (3.22) and cannot see a 2S mid tap; with a mid-cell pull-down an open wire reads cell 1 near 0 V, CUV turns DSG off and its recovery needs min cell >= 3750 mV with charging, which never holds (inference, as V301 allows)

requirements.name: pack voltage
requirements.required: 8.45 V; 25.2 V continuous; 37.3 V clamp for up to 10 us held at or under the pin rating
requirements.datasheet: BAT, VCC, PBI, PACK, SMBC, SMBD 30 V absolute (7.1), 26 V recommended for PACK and the SMBus pins, 2.2 V to 26 V for BAT and VCC (7.3): 8.45 V and 25.2 V hold; the 35.7 V (27 degC) to 37.3 V (125 degC) clamp level for up to 10 us is above the 30 V absolute rating, so each pin takes the series resistor and capacitor of the pin requirement below (the BQ40Z80 states 35 V absolute)

requirements.name: overcurrent threshold
requirements.required: 61.08 mV on 1 mOhm; window above 52.1 A and at or below 90 A, untrimmed and post-trim, shunt within +0.5 %
requirements.datasheet: VOCD -16.6 to -100 mV in 5.56 mV steps (RSNS = 1), VOFFSET +/-2.5 mV post-trim, VSCALE +/-10 % no trim and +/-5 % post-trim (7.31): 61.08 mV on 1 mOhm trips at 52.47 A to 69.69 A untrimmed and 55.53 A to 66.63 A post-trim; with the shunt 0.5 % high the untrimmed lower edge is 52.21 A, above 52.1 A; 0.5 % low puts the upper edge at 70.04 A, under 90 A (arithmetic); the firmware OCD1 and OCD2 fields are disabled

requirements.name: short circuit
requirements.datasheet: SCD1 -44.4 to -200 mV in 22.2 mV steps: 111.0 mV on 1 mOhm trips at 103.0 A to 119.1 A

requirements.name: charge overvoltage
requirements.datasheet: COV thresholds 0 to 32767 mV (default 4300 mV)

requirements.name: pack temperature
requirements.required: NTC 10 kOhm B 3435 K; 55 degC charge and discharge, 0 degC discharge, 10 degC charge; calibrated to about +/-1 K; reported
requirements.datasheet: TS1 to TS4 with an 18 kOhm internal pull-up (14.4 to 21.6 kOhm, 7.22); OTC, OTD, UTC and UTD protections in data flash: UTC Threshold -400 to 1500 in 0.1 degC (set 100 for 10 degC), delay 0 to 255 s; Temperature() over SMBus; the calibration and the B 3435 K fit are board steps (V310); that the default thermistor coefficients fit B 3435 K is not stated in the documents read

data.ruling: The refutation stands. The re-rank dropped PTN5110NHQZ under Charger input limit as "not qualified" because its datasheet supposedly gives no sink-side detection thresholds. That is false. PTN5110 Rev. 1.6 (3 April 2020), Table 12, lists two sink-mode CC (configuration channel) thresholds: VTUS at 0.61/0.66/0.70 V and VTUM at 1.16/1.23/1.31 V (min/typ/max). These are the USB Type-C limits that separate the three source advertisements a sink reads across its Rd. Below VTUS is default current, between VTUS and VTUM is 1.5 A, and above VTUM is 3 A. So the datasheet covers all three levels the requirement names (IOBoard.md, Charger input limit; Research.md R7). The verifier said a separate 3 A sink threshold is missing. A sink needs none, because the 3 A advertisement is the range above VTUM. That remark does not weaken the refutation. The re-rank's other reasons are not drop grounds. A unit price of 9.7653 is no gate in the Sourcing rules. The schema.org BackOrder flag on NXP's page is not a lifecycle status: the same page reads "Status - Active", which passes the Lifecycle check. The register definitions in references [3] and [5] stay not read. A gap in reading does not show a missing threshold. The drop's reason fails, so PTN5110NHQZ goes back to the function's candidates. Whether a TCPC (Type-C port controller), which firmware reads over I²C to set the charger's limit, ranks above the current part (FUSB303BTMX) is a ranking question this figure does not decide. The ruling concerns this function's requirement values, not the part's lifecycle or identity.

data.ruling: The refutation stands. The drop's main reason is that the data sheet states only the source pull-up currents, so detection of Default, 1.5 A and 3.0 A at the sink is not shown. That premise is false. PTN5110 Rev. 1.6 (3 April 2020), Table 12, page 38, states two sink-mode detection thresholds next to the Ipullup rows. VTUS, "Standard current mode detection threshold, Sink mode", is 0.61 / 0.66 / 0.70 V (minimum / typical / maximum). VTUM, "Medium current mode detection threshold, Sink mode", is 1.16 / 1.23 / 1.31 V. Section 1 also says the part implements the Type-C CC analog portion, "Rd/Rp/Ra detection". The two thresholds split the CC voltage at the sink into three bands: below VTUS, between VTUS and VTUM, and above VTUM. That is a separate band for each of Default, 1.5 A and 3.0 A. So the verifier's further point that no 3.0 A sink threshold is stated is wrong too: VTUM is the boundary to the 3.0 A band. The band reading rests on the data sheet's labels only; the USB Type-C specification is not in the tree and was not read. The register coding (CC_STATUS) is deferred to the TCPC (Type-C Port Controller) specification [3] and the programming guide [5]. Neither was read, so how firmware reads the level is not read. That does not bring back the stated premise. None of the drop's "Also" items is a rule failure. JLCPCB stock is 600 with a presale count of 581. That clears the S4 gate: the need is 5 boards × 1 placement, so the gate is the floor of 50. The NXP page lists the status as Active, which passes S5. Its schema availability "BackOrder" is not a lifecycle status. A price of 9.7653 a unit and the need for a TCPM (Type-C Port Manager) stack are ranking factors, not requirement or sourcing failures. The refutation concerns this function's requirement, the input limit's advertisement detection, so its scope is function.

data.ruling: The datasheet verifier's refutation stands for the transient half of V112. The value says no page states a transient at the servo converter's VIN or its duration, and records it as not read. Research.md at 68adf31, which this run reads, does state one. Line 591 (Follow-ups, input transient clamp) puts 60 V for 10 us on the input. TVS2701DRBR clamps it to 35.7 V at 27 degC and 37.3 V at 125 degC. Behind the overvoltage cut-off, the bus carries that voltage to the TPS55285 for 3.98 us typical and 5.4 us maximum, plus the MOSFETs' gate-discharge time. V308 (line 1021) gives the owner's answer of 2026-10-02 in its Answer column: a second clamp on the bus, behind the cut-off and ahead of the TPS55285, holds the TPS55285 input pins at or under 27 V. data.ruling: The refutation stands. V113 asks for the lowest voltage at the servo converter's VIN when it runs from the pack. It asks whether that is 6.0 V, or 6.0 V less a stated drop across the pack path. The value gives 6.0 V at the pack terminals and says the drop across R5's pack path is not read. The owner's V294 answer of 2026-10-02 states the pack-path sizing that the value itself cites: "The pack path stays sized at 6.0 V: 52.1 A nominal at a 5.8 V bus, rated 60 A". The 52.1 A comes from FU-2B1's R5 P2 V90 value, 302.0 W in at a 5.8 V bus (302.0 / 5.8 = 52.07 A). That 302.0 W includes the four TPS55285 inputs (283.7 W). The bus is therefore the node at the converters' VIN, and the owner's sizing puts it at 5.8 V. That is 0.2 V under the 6.0 V pack floor. A stated figure for the drop exists in an owner answer, so the value is wrong to say it is not read. It is also wrong to check the converter from 6.0 V and not from 5.8 V. The rest of the value is right: 6.0 V at the pack terminals (IOBoard.md Pack voltage range) and the 6.6 V under-load floor (V294). The TPS55285 still runs at 5.8 V: SLVSI72A 5.2 gives a VIN range of 2.4 to 22 V for VOUT of 3.0 V or more. The 5.8 V figure changes the low-end input and inductor currents R6 checks, not whether the part is usable. The finding concerns this function's requirement value, not the part.

data.ruling: The refutation holds. Raised by P1 row V134 is filed under "R6, Port supply switch". It asks for the highest current the servo rail may deliver into a shorted port, and it is marked "for research (owner, 2026-09-28)". P2 must find that value and qualify the port switch against it. The current flows through the closed port switch until the port's current limit opens it. The switch's list has 14 entries, and none of them is sourced to V134 or limits a short-circuit or peak current through the switch. Its sources are V55, V114, V277, V282, V302, V122, V116, V124, V126, V312, V125, V136, V127, V123, V130, V133 and V121. The value appears only in the Servo supply list, as "Current into a shorted port". That entry qualifies the TPS55285, not the switch. The Port supply current limit list holds the trip band (3.0 to 6.35 A; 4.30 to 4.51 A for the INA301A1IDGKR). It does not hold the current the switch must carry before the trip opens it. The list is therefore missing one requirement: the switch must carry the shorted-port current until the limit acts. That current is bounded by the 6.35 A output-limit setting with the 128 us OCP_DELAY, and by ILIM_AVG, 7 A minimum and 8 A typical, with no maximum stated. This ruling is about this function's requirement list, not about any part. No part was ruled on. The verifier's note that BUK7K6R8-40E (IDM 276 A at tp up to 10 us) would meet the requirement does not affect the ruling.
